subject: dragonling
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a baby dragon design at a small scale with a big head, stubby legs, small wings, and a tail, planning a quadruped stance and working out the spine chain coordinates starting from the hips.

I'm figuring out separate chains for spine, tail, and neck using catmull-rom paths with appropriate parenting, then planning the skull, snout, jaw, eyes, and horns to build out the head.

Now I'm working out the four limbs, defining shoulder/hip and foot positions, bend directions for front versus hind legs, and checking that leg reach exceeds the actual joint distance so the poses work.

I'm adding simple foot geometry with spike claws for toes, deciding chain parenting so hind legs attach to the hips joint and front legs to the upper spine, and naming joints like hipHL/hipHR based on side. Now I'm starting to think through a small wing structure attached via an arm chain.

Writing wing chain code...

Then I'll add a tail: a catmull chain of four points sweeping down and back from the hips, named tail1 etc, parented to hips with role tail.

Tapering the sweep radius and capping the tail tip with a small diamond spade. I'm scattering dorsal spikes along the spine, neck, and tail sweeps using a spike-along-curve helper.

For color, I'm applying a countershade paint (green body fading to cream belly) across body, tail, legs, and neck, with cream horns and orange wing membranes, then adding yellow eyes with black pupils.

Now working out the skull geometry: a scaled sphere for the cranium, a tapered frustum for the snout with nostril spheres, and a hinged lower jaw built from another frustum anchored at a jaw joint below the snout.

I'm checking the vertical gap between the snout bottom and jaw top to avoid overlap, adding a couple of small cone-shaped fangs on the jaw, and placing the eyes using local offsets for left/up/forward relative to the head joint.

Positioning the eye and pupil spheres with slightly different sizes and colors, then adding spike-shaped horns and ear fins projecting from the head using directional offsets, while skipping belly plates for now and setting the foot sphere height to rest on the ground.

I'm tuning the body proportions—setting foot radius and scale so the sole sits at ground level, adjusting spine and neck radii for a rounder belly and tapered neck, and checking overall height comes out to about 0.7 meters with the head topping around 0.67. Now I'm starting to write the spike helper function that builds horn and fin shapes from a base point, direction, length, and radius.

Still writing limb and claw placement logic...
